previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, and bipolar disorder was admitted for worsening abdominal pain, hypoglycemia, and shoulder injury after a fall. The abdominal pain was consistent with acute on chronic pancreatitis, though imaging showed no obstruction or acute surgical findings. He was treated with IV fluids, pain control, and gradual advancement of diet. His blood sugar improved with supportive care, and he was instructed to hold metformin until follow-up and to only take Lantus insulin with full meals. He tolerated oral intake, had stable vital signs, and was discharged home the next day with follow-up instructions and medication adjustments.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with Hx of Chronic Pancreatitis presenting with 4 days 
of abdominal and flank pain, reportedly exactly like his prior 
flares, as well as nausea and vomiting

# Abdominal Pain/Nausea/Vomiting: Given ___ medical 
history and assurance that his current symptoms are exactly like 
his chronic pancreatitis flares, this was likely the same 
process. Unclear trigger - may be related to diet. He denied 
ETOH consumption and fasting lipid profile was normal. Report of 
flank pain was concerning for renal involvement; however, flank 
pain disappeared and urinalysis was negative. He remained 
afebrile and lactate was normal. Abdominal exam without 
peritoneal signs. No imaging was performed. He was placed on 
bowel rest, given intravenous hydration, and pain control with 
IV Dilaudid 1 mg q3h. His diet was advanced and pain medication 
switched to an oral regimen. He tolerated regular foods and was 
discharged home with instructions to schedule a follow up with 
his Primary Care Physician. He was not given any narcotics. He 
was continued on his outpatient regimen of Gabapentin 400 TID, 
Omeprazole 20 BID, and Ranitidine 150 daily, as well as 
Pancreatic enzyme supplement TID.
